regulatory_and_risk_profile: Zero data retention (ZDR) and bring-your-own keys
Model Risk Management validation before any production use
paper_process_blockers: InfoSec review must run in parallel with the proof of value, not after it
Legal redlines on the data processing agreement take 90 days or more
Procurement needs a named budget owner before it issues a PO
Model Risk Management must sign off on any model used in credit or fraud decisions
dominant_friction: Risk committees block anything they cannot audit, even when the business case is strong.
value_frame: Lead with deterministic auditability, private VPC or ZDR architecture, and parallel InfoSec timelines before the proof of value completes.

buying_committee.primary_fear: We approve a model we cannot validate, reproduce, or defend to examiners.
Another pilot becomes shelfware that we must support forever.
A model leaks customer data through a sub-processor nobody reviewed.
An unexplained AI decision in a credit or fraud case becomes a regulatory finding.

signature_objections: Our CISO will not sign until zero data retention is written into the data processing agreement. Can you commit to that on paper this quarter?
If the model hallucinates a credit decision, who carries the liability, you or us?
We have a 90-day agreement review cycle. Can your proof of value finish before our lawyers finish reading?

metrics.speaker: Head of Model Risk (MRM)
metrics.setup: From a model risk view, the fraud queue is where this gets judged.
metrics.partial: We track false positives on the fraud queue, but nobody has agreed a target, and missed fraud cannot go up.
metrics.verbatim: Below 2 percent false positives, with no rise in missed fraud. If the agent cannot hit that, we do not move forward.

economic_buyer.speaker: CIO
economic_buyer.setup: I like what I am hearing, and I can get this moving on the platform side.
economic_buyer.partial: My platform group holds the budget, but anything above our approval cap needs a co-signer.
economic_buyer.verbatim: Up to the cap, I sign the PO myself from the platform budget. Above it, the Chief Risk Officer has the final sign-off.

decision_criteria.speaker: CISO
decision_criteria.setup: We are looking at three vendors, and security has a long checklist this time: zero retention, encryption keys, audit logs.
decision_criteria.partial: Security and model risk weight that checklist differently, so there is no single tie-breaker yet.
decision_criteria.verbatim: Failing zero data retention. That is out on day one, whatever the price. After that we score sub-processor disclosure, bring-your-own keys and audit logs.

decision_process.speaker: CIO
decision_process.setup: If the proof of value works, we will want to move quickly.
decision_process.partial: Day one is a committee review. After that it goes to legal and a sign-off, but the order changes.
decision_process.verbatim: After the committee: InfoSec, then Model Risk, then legal redlines, then procurement signs. Legal alone takes about 90 days.

paper_process.speaker: CISO
paper_process.setup: InfoSec reviews every new vendor before anything goes live, and that includes a proof of value.
paper_process.partial: Possibly. But legal will also want redlines on the data processing agreement, and that takes a while.
paper_process.verbatim: Ninety days minimum. If you want to be live this quarter, InfoSec has to start in parallel with your proof of value.

identify_pain.speaker: Head of Model Risk (MRM)
identify_pain.setup: My analysts are buried in false positive fraud alerts, and the last audit noticed.
identify_pain.partial: A lot of hours. Most of the alerts they clear turn out to be nothing, and the audit findings keep stacking up.
identify_pain.verbatim: We already have forty-one open findings on manual alert review, and I cannot keep adding analysts to close them.

champion.speaker: Head of Model Risk (MRM)
champion.setup: The risk committee will have to approve this, and the examiners will look at it after them.
champion.partial: I think it would help my team, and I am willing to push it. I am less sure what the examiners will want.
champion.verbatim: A validation pack I can defend in front of the examiners. With that, I will take this to the risk committee myself.

competition.speaker: CIO
competition.setup: I should be honest: we have other options on the table.
competition.partial: Building it ourselves is unlikely. But our platform group already licenses a cloud provider's built-in option.
competition.verbatim: That cloud-native option is the benchmark. You have to beat its price and its auditability.

veto_holder.reason: No model reaches production without a validation pack they can defend to examiners.

metrics.open: What number has to move on the fraud queue for this to be worth it, and by when?
metrics.pin: How much do you need to cut false positives this year without raising missed fraud?

economic_buyer.open: Who signs the PO for a platform like this, and up to what amount?
economic_buyer.pin: Above that cap, whose budget does this come out of, and who has the final sign-off?

decision_criteria.open: How will you score vendors on zero retention, keys and audit logs? Which criterion breaks a tie?
decision_criteria.pin: What would rule us out on day one, regardless of price?

decision_process.open: After a successful proof of value, what happens on day one, day ten and day thirty?
decision_process.pin: Who else needs to approve after the committee? Walk me through the approval path.

paper_process.open: Can InfoSec start reviewing in parallel with the proof of value, not after it?
paper_process.pin: How long do legal redlines on the data processing agreement usually take here?

identify_pain.open: What does a false positive cost you in analyst hours each month?
identify_pain.pin: What happens if you do nothing and the audit findings keep stacking up?

champion.open: If I am not in the room, how would you make the case to the risk committee?
champion.pin: What would you need to take this to the examiners and the committee with confidence?

competition.open: What happens if you build this in-house, or do nothing?
competition.pin: What are you comparing us against, including what your platform group already licenses?

account_research.strong: I saw fraud operations moved under the CIO last quarter. What prompted that?

discovery_questioning.strong: Walk me through how an alert gets worked today, start to finish.

listening_summarizing.strong: So the real cost is analyst hours, not missed fraud. Did I get that right?

commercial_insight.strong: Banks like yours lose more to alert fatigue than to missed fraud. Here is the number.

value_messaging.strong: Today, 4 hours per case. After, 20 minutes, proven with a bank your size.

answer_first.strong: My recommendation: start with fraud operations. Three reasons.

identify_pain.strong: What does a false positive cost you in analyst hours each month?

champion.strong: If I am not in the room, how would you make the case to your CRO?

paper_process.speaker: CISO
paper_process.setup: The pilot cleared InfoSec, but production is a new review. Live customer data changes the scope.
paper_process.partial: We can open it early. The production review also covers data residency and audit log retention.
paper_process.verbatim: Eight weeks for the production review, and residency has to be signed off first. Start it now and you make the quarter.

decision_process.speaker: CIO
decision_process.setup: The pilot workload is live. Now three other business lines want it, and each one counts as a new use case.
decision_process.partial: Each new use case goes back through Model Risk, then a change board. Nobody has mapped the order for an expansion.
decision_process.verbatim: Model Risk validates each use case first, then the change board, then the business line head signs. About six weeks per use case.

economic_buyer.speaker: CIO
economic_buyer.setup: Expanding to three business lines is a different budget conversation from the pilot.
economic_buyer.partial: The pilot came from my platform budget. An expansion across business lines needs a shared funding line.
economic_buyer.verbatim: The business lines fund their own usage, and the Chief Risk Officer signs anything that spans more than one. I approve the platform layer.

competition.speaker: CIO
competition.setup: Now that it works, our cloud provider is offering to run the same workload natively, at cost.
competition.partial: Their native option is tempting. My platform team also thinks they could rebuild it on the provider's tools.
competition.verbatim: We would compare you against the native option at cost, plus a rebuild by my team. You need to win on auditability and run cost per alert.

metrics.speaker: Head of Model Risk (MRM)
metrics.setup: Before anyone signs a bigger commit, I want the production numbers, not the pilot numbers.
metrics.partial: The pilot hit its false positive target. In production we also report alerts per analyst, across all three business lines, to the examiners.
metrics.verbatim: Alerts per analyst down by half across all three lines within two quarters, with false positives held under the pilot rate.

identify_pain.speaker: Head of Model Risk (MRM)
identify_pain.setup: Usage on the first line has gone flat, and I have to explain why to the committee.
identify_pain.partial: Analysts trust it for simple alerts but still clear complex ones by hand. So the savings stalled.
identify_pain.verbatim: We are paying for the platform and still staffing the complex queue in full. That is two cost bases, and the committee sees both.

paper_process.open: Can InfoSec start reviewing for production now, in parallel with the pilot?
paper_process.pin: How long does the production review take once residency and audit log retention are in scope?

decision_process.open: For each new use case, what are the steps from the live pilot to production?
decision_process.pin: Who else needs to approve after Model Risk and the change board? Walk me through the approval path.

economic_buyer.open: For the expansion across business lines, whose budget does this come from?
economic_buyer.pin: Who signs the shared funding line, and who has the final sign-off across business lines?

competition.open: Would you run it natively with the provider, or do nothing and keep the workload where it is?
competition.pin: What are you comparing us against: their native option, or a rebuild by your platform team?

metrics.open: Which number must hold in production before you sign anything bigger?
metrics.pin: How much do you need to cut alerts per analyst across the three lines, and by when?

identify_pain.open: What does the flat usage cost you each month?
identify_pain.pin: What happens if you do nothing and analysts keep clearing complex alerts by hand?
